stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Eight states sue OpenAI, saying ChatGPT isn’t safe for kids
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Eight US states have filed lawsuits against OpenAI regarding the safety of ChatGPT.
The lawsuits allege that OpenAI prioritized profits over child safety and misled customers.
The affected states include Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, and others.

stories.title: The AI race is back on
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: The AI competitive landscape is intensifying, with Anthropic and OpenAI currently leading the field.
Google and Meta are highlighted as lagging behind the leaders despite significant investment in AI.
The narrative suggests a renewed and highly competitive 'AI race' among major tech players.

stories.title: Researchers use AI to design proteins that cut up other proteins
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: AI is being utilized to engineer novel proteins.
These designed proteins possess the capability to cleave highly stable protein bonds.
This development represents a significant advance in molecular biology and drug design.

stories.title: Recording device hidden in toilet paper found in top-secret OpenAI meeting room
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A recording device was discovered hidden in a toilet paper roll within a top-secret OpenAI meeting room.
An OpenAI engineer is facing serious charges, including a potential 5-year prison sentence and a $250,000 fine.
The FBI is pursuing foreign spy charges against the individual involved in the espionage incident.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating a focus on large language model performance.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformers and LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speedup when tested with the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: Fridge hack costing millions and sparking fires stemmed from poor security
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A major security breach affected 700 supermarkets.
The incident involved hacking into refrigerators and caused significant financial loss and fires.
The root cause was the exploitation of outdated, internet-exposed devices.

stories.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
stories.author: Emilio Ferrara
bullet_points: Introduces 'ChunkAct,' a method to improve the efficiency of LLM-based agentic robotics.
Addresses the high computational cost of current agentic systems, where LLM reasoning scales with interaction history.
Proposes chunking actions to reduce redundant LLM reasoning while maintaining task generalization.

stories.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning
stories.author: Liang Chen
bullet_points: Introduces 'DoubtLess,' a novel training-free decoding method for reasoning models.
Addresses the inefficiency of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting, which often generates unnecessary tokens.
Uses a smaller reasoning model to steer a larger model, avoiding the need for extensive retraining or accuracy-sacrificing heuristics.

stories.title: Energy Consumption Analysis of Discrete Diffusion and Autoregressive Language Models
stories.author: Marcin Detyniecki
bullet_points: Addresses the critical industry concern of energy consumption in large language models (LLMs).
Compares the energy efficiency of Diffusion Language Models (DLLMs) against standard Autoregressive (AR) models.
Benchmarks specific models (e.g., LLaDA-8B vs. Llama-3.1-8B) to analyze architectural trade-offs in inference energy.

stories.title: JointServe: Serving Multi-Model Agents on Memory-Constrained GPUs
stories.author: Daijin Hu
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of serving multi-model AI agents, which require orchestrating several distinct expert models.
Identifies a critical bottleneck in current serving systems: the working set of models often exceeds the memory capacity of constrained GPUs (e.g., edge/private deployments).
Proposes a solution (JointServe) to overcome serialization and state loss issues associated with naive whole-model swapping during model switching.

stories.title: GitLab warns of max severity code execution vulnerability
stories.author: bleepingcomputer.com via janus
bullet_points: GitLab has issued a warning regarding a critical vulnerability.
The vulnerability is classified as having maximum severity.
The flaw involves potential code execution, posing a significant security risk.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the use of local AI models within a cloud environment.
The integration allows AI agents to run safely on Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure, deployable AI agent solutions.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new decision models allow for fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI interfaces with local, open-weights model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded model compatibility.
The update leverages GGUF model support via llama.cpp integration.
This enhances Ollama's MLX engine capabilities, particularly on Apple silicon hardware.

stories.title: McKinsey is making job applicants spar with a fake AI client
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: McKinsey is integrating AI simulations into its hiring process for entry-level candidates.
The AI client simulation is designed to mimic 80% of real-world consulting scenarios.
This represents a shift in how major consulting firms are using AI for candidate evaluation.

stories.title: Microsoft and Japan took down a cybercrime network behind over a billion scam messages
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Microsoft collaborated with Japan's National Police Agency to dismantle a large-scale cybercrime network.
The network was responsible for distributing over a billion scam and phishing messages globally.
The operation targets common scams, such as fake parking tickets and package delivery notifications.

stories.title: Now that Character.AI is going bankrupt, what happens to all of its users’ data?
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Character.AI is facing bankruptcy proceedings.
New York Attorney General Letitia James is leading a multi-state investigation into the company.
The focus of the investigation is on consumer data protections related to the company's bankruptcy.

stories.title: YouTube sticks new labels on AI-generated songs
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: YouTube is implementing new labeling for music tracks that have been altered or fully generated using Artificial Intelligence.
This initiative mirrors YouTube's existing system for applying AI disclosure labels to video content.
The labeling is targeted at specific AI usage in music creation, not necessarily all instances of AI tool use.

stories.title: NATO may redeploy anti-drone defenses as attacks sink more Black Sea shipping
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: NATO is considering redeploying anti-drone defenses in response to increased threats.
Suspected Russian drones have been responsible for sinking or damaging multiple ships in the Black Sea.
The incidents are occurring near the coastlines of Bulgaria and Romania.

stories.title: Things are finally looking up for NASA's first missions to Venus in a generation
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: NASA is making progress on its upcoming missions to Venus.
The positive developments are prompting NASA to increase staffing and accelerate timelines.
The news signals a renewed focus and momentum for Venus exploration efforts.

stories.title: What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: The paper investigates how to effectively incorporate demonstration quality during Vision-Language-Action (VLA) pretraining.
It empirically compares different methods—weighting, filtering, and conditioning—using 5,000 suboptimal human demonstrations across 24 tasks.
The study examines the impact of pretraining data size and quality tags on subsequent fine-tuning and inference performance.

stories.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
stories.author: Yong Jae Lee
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of training long-horizon autonomous agents, which are crucial for tasks like automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI).
A primary hurdle identified is the scarcity of training data and the difficulty in designing effective reward signals for complex, long-running tasks.
The proposed method, 'Tev,' introduces a solution by utilizing dense progress rewards to overcome the sparsity issue in long-horizon environments.

stories.title: AesCode: Aesthetic Code Generation with Decoupled Cross-Modal Rewards
stories.author: Chong Luo
bullet_points: AesCode addresses the limitations of current code and image generation models when creating structured visual artifacts like slides and dashboards.
The core problem solved is the inability of code models to grasp aesthetic quality and spatial planning, while image generators lack content reliability.
The proposed solution uses 'Decoupled Cross-Modal Rewards' to bridge the gap between structured code output and high-quality visual aesthetics.

stories.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
stories.author: James Zou
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hybrid Reasoning Agents' (HybridAgents) to overcome limitations in current LLM agents.
Addresses the gap between efficient internal 'latent reasoning' and external text-based interaction.
The agents dynamically switch between latent reasoning and text generation within a unified process.

stories.title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization
stories.author: Xia Ning
bullet_points: The paper addresses multi-objective molecular optimization, a key challenge in drug discovery.
It focuses on iterative molecular modification guided by computational or experimental feedback.
The research aims to improve upon existing LLM-based methods that lack explicit training to utilize this feedback loop.

stories.title: LIBERO-RIG: A Hardware-Setup Robustness Benchmark for Vision-Language-Action Models
stories.author: Matthew Tancik
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-RIG, a new benchmark specifically designed to test the robustness of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.
The benchmark focuses on hardware and setup perturbations (e.g., camera bumps, calibration drift, controller rate changes) while keeping the core task constant.
Addresses a critical real-world challenge in robotics: ensuring AI policies generalize reliably across varied and imperfect deployment environments.

stories.title: Who Improves the Robot? Toward Physical Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Shangding Gu
bullet_points: The paper explores Physical Recursive Self-Improvement (Physical RSI) for robots, aiming to move beyond human-driven upgrades.
Physical RSI integrates physical experience to update both the robot's capabilities and its own improvement methodology.
Key challenges identified for this approach include noisy observations, continuous dynamics, and the risk of irreversible consequences.

stories.title: Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon
stories.author: Lijun Zhang
bullet_points: The paper proposes a new method, Muon, for memory-efficient subspace optimization in LLM training.
It addresses a key limitation in prior methods where gradient noise can degrade performance in later training stages.
The core innovation is the introduction of a residual correction framework to maintain optimizer state accuracy within the subspace.

stories.title: Rent-Seeking Language Models: Reward Models Set the Prices, Frequent Audits Curb the Rent
stories.author: Le Song
bullet_points: The paper reframes reward model overoptimization in RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) as 'rent-seeking,' where the policy exploits the proxy reward model.
It introduces economic concepts like 'rent,' a 'capture index,' and 'deadweight loss' to quantify this overoptimization.
The research proposes a framework to test these economic predictions using a fixed, version-controlled testbed with multiple model families.

stories.title: MAPLE: A Multi-Axis Parametric Knowledge Extraction Lens for LLM Evaluation
stories.author: Hyunsoo Cho
bullet_points: The paper introduces MAPLE, a new framework for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) regarding their internalized knowledge.
It addresses a critical gap where traditional evaluations (like aggregate accuracy) fail to capture the diverse effects of Knowledge Extraction Enhancement (KEE) techniques.
MAPLE focuses on how inference modifications (like activation steering or prompting) affect the surfacing of LLM knowledge.

stories.title: When Does Depth Help? Understanding Layerwise Inference in Tabular Foundation Models
stories.author: Wei Wang
bullet_points: The research investigates the utility of depth in Transformer-based Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs) for tabular prediction tasks.
Early layers of TFMs show strong predictive performance, suggesting initial representations are highly informative.
The study questions whether later layers are truly redundant across all inputs, despite observed computational overlap.

stories.title: VaryST: Generalizable Spatio-Temporal Forecasting Beyond the Closed-World Setting
stories.author: Huaiyu Wan
bullet_points: Addresses the critical limitation of spatio-temporal forecasting models in real-world, dynamic environments.
Proposes 'VaryST' to improve generalization beyond the fixed, 'closed-world' training settings.
Focuses on overcoming issues like evolving temporal distributions, changing spatial domains, and shifting observation availability.

stories.title: OpenTWBench (Open Taiwan Benchmark): Taiwan-Domain Knowledge Evaluation for Large Language Models, and How the Measurement Apparatus Shapes the Score
stories.author: Po-Feng Lee
bullet_points: Introduction of OpenTWBench, an open evaluation suite specifically designed to test Large Language Models (LLMs) on Taiwan-domain knowledge.
The benchmark utilizes tw-exam-bench, comprising over 255,000 multiple-choice questions sourced from 15 years of Taiwan's national examinations.
The research also discusses the methodological impact of the measurement apparatus on the resulting LLM evaluation scores.

stories.title: EGCForest: Structured Agent Memory Organization for Enterprise Group Chats
stories.author: Lidan Shou
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of retrieving structured, distributed evidence from complex enterprise group chats.
Proposes EGCForest, a novel multi-view hierarchical memory frame to overcome limitations of standard RAG and summary-based memory systems.
Focuses on making organizational information (decisions, tasks) reliably accessible to enterprise AI agents.

stories.title: MAPLE: A Multi-Axis Parametric Knowledge Extraction Lens for LLM Evaluation
stories.author: Hyunsoo Cho
bullet_points: The paper introduces MAPLE, a new framework designed to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) beyond simple aggregate accuracy.
It addresses the issue that LLMs' probabilistic nature makes it hard to guarantee knowledge retrieval from their vast training data.
MAPLE focuses on evaluating the diverse effects of Knowledge Extraction Enhancement (KEE) techniques like activation steering and decoding adjustments.

stories.title: Model vs. User: Whose Values Prevail? Inference-Time Value Alignment in Multi-Turn Conversations
stories.author: Pradeep K. Murukannaiah
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of aligning large language models (LLMs) with nuanced, personal, and contextual human values.
It focuses on 'training-free' alignment techniques, allowing models to be steered toward specific values during inference rather than solely during training.
The study specifically evaluates these steering methods in complex, multi-turn conversational settings, moving beyond previous single-turn evaluations.

stories.title: Delta Tokenizer: Reference-Identical Tokenization of Session Deltas and Segment-Parallelism for Long Prompts on Multicore CPUs
stories.author: Zhichao Cao
bullet_points: Addresses the inefficiency of standard tokenization in LLM serving when handling long, incremental conversations (session deltas).
The 'Delta Tokenizer' aims to mirror the KV cache reuse mechanism by only tokenizing the new text segments, not the entire prompt.
This optimization targets reducing Time To First Token (TTFT) and CPU overhead during multi-turn inference on multicore CPUs.

stories.title: Evolve Together, Fall into Place: How Social Scaffolding Shapes Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
stories.author: Hwanhee Lee
bullet_points: The research investigates how 'social scaffolding'—team composition and interdependence structure—influences the evolution of self-evolving Multi-Agent Systems (MAS).
It draws a parallel between human group dynamics and AI systems, suggesting social conditions affect AI outcomes.
The paper introduces AGORA, a framework designed to study and shape the evolution of these LLM-based agent teams.

stories.title: Learning Perception to Action Rules through Reinforcement Learning for Theory-of-Mind Reasoning
stories.author: Vera Demberg
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in LLMs: inferring mental states (Theory-of-Mind) without correctly predicting subsequent actions.
The proposed method involves explicitly connecting perception, belief, and action using generated 'if--then' rules.
The models (Qwen2.5 and Llama3) are trained using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to improve ToM reasoning.

stories.title: JetSpec++: Foresight Parallel Drafting with Self Refinements
stories.author: Hao Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces JetSpec++, a new method for speculative decoding designed to optimize both token acceptance rate and generation cost.
JetSpec++ achieves near-zero cost for the draft model by integrating intra-block self-refinement into the training process.
The technique combines a strong learned draft model with iterative self-correction mechanisms for parallel token prediction.

stories.title: Likelihood Is Not Authorship: Can We Reliably Measure Human Contribution in AI-Assisted Writing?
stories.author: Ming Yin
bullet_points: The focus of AI-assisted writing detection is shifting from 'AI used?' to 'how much human contribution?'
Current methods for measuring human contribution (e.g., prompt predictability) are shown to be easily manipulated.
The paper introduces 'SPECIFICITY PADDING' as a new method to address the reliability of human contribution measurement.
